found.location: §The hardware probe picks your model, line 197
found.issue: "The dictionary that drives this defines four tiers, from a small model that fits an 8 GB GPU up to a mixture-of-experts model for the largest cards." On Windows an 8 GB dedicated GPU does not land on the smallest tier. crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:131-177 makes tier 0 Gemma 4 E2B and 179-196 makes tier 1 Gemma 4 E4B at 4,977,171,584 bytes. objectives_source: Derived by the reviewer. tasks/docs/artifacts/T2.research.json carries `objectives: []`, and wiki/clients/windows.md records none in its frontmatter, so no stage upstream of this one wrote down what the page is for. The six below are what the page plainly sets out to teach, read from its section spine and its opening, and levelled against the table in the hearth-style skill. They are proposed rather than ratified, and the orchestrator should either adopt them or replace them, because a platform overview with no recorded objectives cannot be checked for content that serves none.

objective_gaps.objective: decide whether your Windows machine can run Hearth
objective_gaps.why: The page has no `What it needs` section and states no floor of any kind: no memory or VRAM minimum, no free-disk figure, no verified Windows version, and no statement that Hearth declines to install on a machine that is too small. §The hardware probe picks your model describes how the machine is sized but names only the 16 GB case, so a reader below that has nothing to measure themselves against. The other four client pages all answer this: wiki/clients/macos.md:31-47 gives four facts, and wiki/clients/ios.md:128, android.md:218 and visionos.md:171 each carry the section. This is the single largest reader gap on the page and it is finding F2.

objective_gaps.objective: name what Hearth on Windows cannot do yet
objective_gaps.why: Partially taught, and nowhere gathered. The limits exist on the page but are scattered into sections about other subjects: the missing in-app updater sits at the end of §Updates, the voice being unavailable until its environment installs sits at the end of §What the installer gives you, and §Status carries only a pre-alpha notice and a dated decision. A reader cannot find the limits by scanning, which is the whole purpose of the spine's honest-limits section. This is finding F9.

Correctly not taught here, recorded so the gap is not read as an oversight. wiki/page-types.md:243-245 keeps installation off a platform overview, and wiki/whats-not-here.md:23-25 registers the missing Windows install guide as a known gap. As of this run the page links Installing Hearth from its opening as well as its foot (F5), so the reader reaches the task in one screen. The corpus-level gap stands: wiki/installing.md is the page that survives T16, and whether it is parameterized by platform or joined by a Windows guide is not this page's decision.

objective_gaps.objective: explain how Hearth chooses a model for your machine
objective_gaps.why: Taught in §The hardware probe picks your model, and materially better after this run. The false 8 GB tier claim is gone (F3) and the take-turns consequence is stated (F4), so a reader now learns what the plan decides, what it tells them, and what a machine that cannot hold both actually feels like. What is still missing is any threshold, which is a deliberate open question rather than an omission: tasks/docs/artifacts/T2.research.json records that no source in the tree names a graphics card inside the take-turns band.

objective_gaps.objective: describe what the Hearth desktop app does on Windows
objective_gaps.why: Taught, but at a cost the reader pays. §What the desktop app is runs about 1135 words with no H3 and carries nine bolded-lead paragraphs, so the material is present and hard to retrieve. Owned by tracker row T15 and already reported by scripts/lint_wiki.py, so it is deliberately absent from found[] and carries no detraction here.

objective_gaps.objective: describe what the installer puts on your machine
objective_gaps.why: Taught in §What the installer gives you, and the install-root default is now correct after T2. The section teaches more than the objective asks, which is finding F1.

objective_gaps.objective: CONTENT SERVING NO OBJECTIVE: the supervised process tree and its port numbers
objective_gaps.why: The fenced tree at lines 175-184 lists five processes with ports 18765, 18766, 18080, 18700 and 18702. No objective a platform overview carries needs a port number: a reader deciding whether to use this client does not, and a reader debugging one is on a different page. wiki/page-types.md:249-251 sends port tables to a reference page. Recorded here rather than charged a second time, because it is the same shape defect as F1 and double-counting it would inflate the score.

objective_gaps.objective: CONTENT SERVING NO OBJECTIVE: the file-tool behavior at lines 128-146
objective_gaps.why: Two paragraphs describe `read_file`, `list_dir`, `write_file`, the allow-listed roots in `file_roots.yaml`, the permission card, its five-minute wait, and grants recorded in `file_grants.yaml`. None of that is Windows-specific: it is harness behavior a persona has on every client, and it would read identically on the macOS page. It serves no objective this page carries, and it is a strong candidate for a concept page under wiki/features/ that all five client pages link to. It sits inside the section T15 owns, so it is recorded rather than charged.

detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline penalty is the sum of all ten found[] detractions: F1 type-mixture 1, F2 missing-spine 2, F3 stale-claim 1, F4 under-informs 1, F5 no-abstract 1, F6 term-list-as-prose 1, F7 missing-figure 1, F8 stale-claim 1, F9 status-log 1, F10 notation nit 0.5, total 10.5. 10 - 10.5 = -0.5, so score_before is the floor, 1. Open penalty is the sum of remaining[]: F1 1 + F2 2 + F8 1 + F9 1 = 5, so score_after is 10 - 5 = 5, and score_delta is +4. Two detractions deviate from the vocabulary table in the hearth-style skill and both are argued rather than assumed. F1 is charged 1 instead of the table's 2 for type-mixture, because the material is accurate where it sits and no reader of this page is misled by it; the cost is corpus-level duplication, and the identical shape at wiki/clients/macos.md:49-87 means the rule and the pages disagree rather than the page being wrong on its own. F6 is charged 1 instead of the table's 2 for term-list-as-prose, because it is a single sentence rather than a run of paragraphs and the reader is not performing the steps by hand. F4 uses the id `under-informs`, which is not in the published vocabulary; the closest entry, stale-claim, is defined as a statement the source tree contradicts, and this sentence is not contradicted, it is incomplete. The vocabulary has no id for a page that names a mechanism and withholds the consequence, and it is worth one, because that is the failure mode a cautious correction produces. Note that score_before is a floor and not a measurement: the true baseline penalty of 10.5 means the page's opening grade would have been negative, so the +4 delta understates the six findings cleared. The verdict of FAIL at 5 reflects what is still open rather than the quality of the prose, and three of the four open items are owned by rows other than T2.
detailed_review.what_worked: Two corrections now hold that a reader can act on. F3 removed a false hardware claim: the page told a reader with an 8 GB graphics card to expect the smallest model, when crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:107-109 says in as many words that an 8 GB Mac and an 8 GB graphics card are different problems, and the derivation in the research artifact puts that card a tier higher. F4 answered the question the orchestrator's correction had left hanging. Dropping the machine class from the coexistence sentence was the right call, since nothing in the tree names a card inside the take-turns band, but the sentence was left promising that the plan would say something without saying what, so "you know what to expect" was exactly what the reader did not get. The consequence is now on the page in the reader's terms, taken from the warning string at plan.rs:144-147, with no figure invented. F5 moved the install entry point from line 234 to the first screen, which is where wiki/clients/macos.md:27-29 puts it, so a reader who came to install no longer has to read a platform overview to find out that the install is documented elsewhere. F6 turned a 77-word sentence with a nested parenthetical into the three ordered stages of first launch. F7 put the page's first figure request on it, for the one settings pane the page describes across two dense paragraphs, and F10 straightened a ragged column in the install-root tree.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: All five points come from four open findings, and only one of them is unowned work this run could plausibly have started. F2 is the big one and the one a reader feels: this page cannot tell anyone whether their Windows machine runs Hearth. There is no memory floor, no GPU floor, no free-disk figure, no Windows version, and no statement that Hearth refuses rather than installing something that cannot run. Every other client page answers that question in one screen, and macOS answers it with four facts. The floor is derivable from source at 4,466,165,856 bytes of memory pool, but the corpus has not settled whether it prints that as 4.47 GB or 4.16 GB, which tracker row T24 still carries, and the disk figures and the verified Windows version exist nowhere in the tree.
